issues.legal_issue: An appellate court cannot decide an appeal on its merits when the appellant does not appear for the hearing.
material_facts: The matter before the High Court was a second appeal.
When the appeal was called for hearing, counsel for the appellants was absent and no request was made on their behalf.
The High Court proceeded to decide the appeal on its merits and dismissed it.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in deciding the appeal on its merits in the appellants’ absence. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and decree and remitted the matter for fresh disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI Rule 17(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, read with its Explanation, permits dismissal for default when the appellant does not appear but does not empower the appellate court to dismiss the appeal on its merits. The Explanation was added by the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976, to clarify that rule. Abdur Rahman v. Athifa Begum and Ghanshyam Dass Gupta v. Makhan Lal confirm that an appellate court cannot decide the merits in the appellant’s absence; doing so deprives the appellant of an opportunity to show sufficient cause for non-appearance.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding before the court was a second appeal.
predicates.appellant_absent_when_called: The appellant or the appellant’s counsel did not appear when the appeal was called for hearing.
predicates.court_decided_appeal_on_merits: The court proceeded to decide the appeal on its merits despite the appellant’s absence.
predicates.merits_decision_must_be_set_aside_and_ca: The merits decision must be set aside and the case sent back for fresh disposal.

issues.definition: When a second appeal is called for hearing in the appellant’s absence and the court decides it on its merits, the merits decision must be set aside and the case remitted for fresh disposal.
